newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds edge up with U.S. mkt, thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds edge up with U.S. mkt, thin trade.

text.p: Argentine bonds were slightly higher late morning Wednesday, following advances in U.S. Treasuries in thin market activity.
A trader said the market was rising on the decline in the 30-year U.S. bond yield and on some short-covering. The 30-year yield fell two basis points to 7.0 percent.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/8 to 93 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was flat at 122.90.
But activity remained in the doldrums, similar to Tuesday, with many players waiting on the sidelines until the release of important U.S. indicators next week.
"The market is quiet with little volume," said another trader.
